label: PYQ-style
stem: List four advantages of genetically modified crops.
model_answer: Any four: more tolerant to abiotic stresses (cold, drought, salt, heat); reduced reliance on chemical pesticides; reduced post-harvest losses; increased efficiency of mineral use; enhanced nutritional value (e.g. Golden rice rich in vitamin A).

label: PYQ-style
stem: What is biopiracy? Give one example involving India.
model_answer: Biopiracy is the use of bio-resources (and traditional knowledge) by multinational companies or organisations without proper authorisation from the countries and people concerned and without compensatory payment. Example: in 1997 an American company was granted a US patent on Basmati rice derived from Indian farmers' varieties (also attempts on turmeric and neem).

scheme.step: Definition with no authorisation and no compensation

label: PYQ-style
stem: Explain how RNA interference has been used to make tobacco plants resistant to the nematode Meloidogyne incognita.
model_answer: Meloidogyne incognita infects tobacco roots and reduces yield. RNAi is a cellular defence in which complementary dsRNA silences a specific mRNA. Nematode-specific genes were introduced into tobacco using Agrobacterium vectors so that the plant made both sense and anti-sense RNA; these formed dsRNA, which silenced the nematode's specific mRNA. The parasite could not survive in the transgenic plant.

scheme.step: Nematode infects roots; RNAi = dsRNA silencing mRNA
Agrobacterium introduces nematode genes; sense + anti-sense → dsRNA
Nematode mRNA silenced; parasite dies; plant protected

label: PYQ-style
stem: *A four-year-old child has repeated serious infections. Tests show that a gene for an enzyme essential to the immune system has been deleted. Doctors consider three options: bone marrow transplant, injecting the missing enzyme, and gene therapy.*

parts.stem: Name the enzyme deficiency and the year of the first clinical gene therapy for it.
What is injecting the missing enzyme called, and why is it not a complete cure?
parts.model_answer: Enzyme replacement therapy; the enzyme is used up and the gene defect remains, so treatment must be repeated.

scheme.step: Enzyme replacement therapy; not curative, repeated

parts.stem: Describe the gene therapy procedure and explain why repeated treatment is needed.
parts.model_answer: Lymphocytes from the child's blood are grown in culture; a functional ADA cDNA is introduced using a retroviral vector; the cells are returned to the child. The engineered lymphocytes are not immortal, so periodic infusions are needed; introducing the gene at an early embryonic stage could give a permanent cure.

scheme.step: Lymphocytes cultured, ADA cDNA via retroviral vector, reinfused

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) Why was insulin from cattle and pigs replaced? Describe how human insulin was produced by recombinant DNA technology. [3]
(b) Give two uses of transgenic animals with an example each. [2]
model_answer:
(a) Animal insulin caused allergy and other reactions in some patients. Insulin has two chains, A and B, joined by disulphide bridges; in the body it is made as pro-insulin with a C peptide. In 1983 Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences coding for chains A and B, introduced them into plasmids of E. coli to make the chains separately, then extracted and combined them by forming disulphide bonds to give human insulin.
(b) Any two: biological products (α-1-antitrypsin for emphysema; Rosie's milk with human α-lactalbumin); disease models (cancer, cystic fibrosis, Alzheimer's); vaccine safety (polio vaccine in mice); chemical toxicity testing; study of normal physiology (insulin-like growth factor).

scheme.step: Structure: A and B chains, disulphide bonds, pro-insulin with C peptide
Eli Lilly: A and B genes in E. coli plasmids, chains joined
